_source: ColdFusion long video, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frame mosaics (0-15 s dense, 16-80 s every 4-6 s, then every ~2 min), 1 s bursts at 16-21 s and 46-51 s, word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (about 175 words a minute). Our own descriptions; shots after 90 s are spot samples. 1.6M views.

hook.firstFrame: black frame; the channel's white logo bars streak in (a 4 s sting)
hook.firstLine: A greeting, then a single dollar figure spoken alone.

shots.picture: logo sting: white slanted bars streak in with a light flare, wordmark forms over grey 3D shapes
a tilted wall of banknote bundles, slow drift; huge white italic '$650 Billion' slides diagonally across
on white, a 3D stack of cash bundles rises; camera tilts up until a space station passes, red '710 km' label lands at an angle
a newspaper analysis page with headline about a $9tn bust, slow scroll
black frame, four aerial photos of named data-centre projects in a row with titles
a business-news headline in white on black, the outlet's name in orange
on white: '140 Data Centers' orange rack icon = '12 GW', camera trucks right as a line draws to a cluster of house icons
aerial footage of half-built data-centre sites and steel frames
satellite image of a construction site in a small window
TV interview of a commentator with a lower-third
conference panels, news clips, phone footage of residents (spot-sampled)
sponsor segment: staged ad footage, product logo card with QR
simple white line chart comparing megaprojects' cost over years, lines labelled at their ends
factory, phone and news footage; a utility bill and text message as evidence; magazine headline; press footage (spot-sampled)
dark outro with light leaks and the closing question

lines.gist: greeting, then the yearly data-centre spending figure of four tech giants
makes the figure physical: a stack of notes taller than the space station's orbit
the plan grows to trillions by the end of the decade
yet nearly half of this year's planned sites are delayed or cancelled
how many projects, how much power, how many homes that equals, a third being built
reports and satellite images contradict the companies' claims of progress
a critic says an announced site is far from finished
the public dislikes data centres too; the question the episode answers is set

ending.cta: asks viewers' views in the comments

whyItWorks: The headline figure is turned into a physical scale picture (a cash stack reaching orbit) within 16 s.
Chains of equivalence: icon = number, then a line draws to a familiar thing (homes), camera trucking along the chain.
Contrast turn at 31 s: huge money in, yet half the projects stalled; the question is set before any background.
Graphics are minimal: white or black ground, one orange accent, condensed italic numerals.
